study_identification_part.si4_title: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study aims to introduce a framework for parsing neuroanatomical subtypes in autism using normative modeling and clustering.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we aim to introduce a novel methodological framework for parsing neuroanatomical subtypes within a large cohort of individuals with autism. ... Specifically, it is necessary to summarize these complex and highly individualized patterns of deviation into a small number of interpretable neurobiological subtypes.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing normative model and cites the original publication (Ref 40) and the dataset description (Ref 41). It briefly summarizes the reference cohort (206 NT, exclusion of ID).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We included 206 neurotypical (NT) (79 female, aged 17.5 ± 6.1 years)... In order to obtain a normative reference, the participants with Intellectual disability were excluded from the NT cohort. ... This sample has been described in detail previously 41 as have the normative models that form the basis for this work 40.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model accounts for age, sex, full-scale IQ, scan quality (Euler number), and site effects (dummy coded).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: we estimated normative models to predict vertex-wise cortical thickness as a function of age and sex plus nuisance covariates including full-scale IQ, plus dummy coded site variables and the Freesurfer Euler number
